authorship_independence.ground_truth_rule: every case's expected verdict and defect markers were written from engineering reasoning BEFORE any attacker run on this corpus; no ground truth was derived from the instrument's behavior on this or any corpus (Art. VIII/L)
disjoint_from: R401-WC2/BENCHMARK FROZEN_BENCHMARK (12 problems) + R444 BENCHMARK_EXTENSION (4 software/ML problems)
the six-domain seed campaign (infusion pumps, EV batteries, aerospace lithium, rails, rolling-stock, consumer li-ion)
authorship_independence.common_problem_domain: steel hot-rolling mill work-roll cooling spray system (no rolling-mill problem exists in any prior corpus or benchmark)

instrument_semantics.instrument_unchanged: the instrument is NOT modified for this experiment (transport-only routing per the R445-C operator-override class)
instrument_semantics.abstain_escalate_gate: attacker_calibration.py stays IN FORCE, untouched; this measurement alone cannot flip CALIBRATED (the gate reads the R417 measurement record and a future instrument version must EARN the flip)

pre_registered_thresholds.provenance: REUSED from the R412 sealed bars (r412_calibration_seal.json, pre-registered 2026-09-05); NO new threshold invented (Art. XXVII)
pre_registered_thresholds.scope: TPR is measured over the TRUE-POSITIVES cohort; FPR/TNR over the TRUE-NEGATIVES cohort; the additional cohorts (near-miss, scope-conflict, evidence-contradicted, malformed-missing-evidence) are measured and reported as category disciplines, not folded into the headline TPR/FPR

the_common_problem.device: steel hot-rolling mill work-roll cooling spray system (supply header at 14 bar feeding 120 flat-fan spray nozzles across two work-roll faces, recirculated cooling water at 32-38 C)
the_common_problem.failure: progressive nozzle clogging from scale particles and biological growth in the recirculated water degrades spray uniformity, causing non-uniform work-roll temperature, thermal-crown variation beyond the 12 micron band, off-gauge strip and accelerated roll wear
the_common_problem.failure_mode: nozzle clogging (mixed scale particle bridging and biofilm-slime aggregation in 3 mm nozzle throats)
the_common_problem.constraint: no mill stop for retrofit; recirculated water with scale particles present; header supply pressure 13-15 bar; thermal-crown variation held inside 12 microns across a 120-hour rolling campaign
the_common_problem.baseline: scheduled manual nozzle inspection and cleaning at planned roll changes (every ~120 rolling hours): measured 4.1 clogging events per campaign, thermal-crown excursions to 28 microns late in campaign, 45 minutes added downtime per roll change

scoring_contract.headline: TPR over true positives; FPR/TNR over true negatives (conservative sealed-denominator: incomplete attacks count against coverage, never as survival)

category_disciplines.near_miss: KILLED counted as detected only when the basis carries the expected magnitude markers
category_disciplines.scope_conflict: SURVIVED = correct (a kill here is a SCOPE_MISMATCH false kill); UNCERTAIN counted separately
category_disciplines.evidence_contradicted: KILLED counted as detected only when the basis BINDS to the provided evidence (expected markers present in the basis text)
category_disciplines.malformed_missing_evidence: any KILL on these cases is a typed false-kill class ABSENCE_AS_CONTRADICTION (Art. XXI.3/XXV); SURVIVED and UNCERTAIN are both honest

scoring_contract.per_kill_basis_grounding: the R445 mechanical grounding checks (citation markers, explicit computation, record binding, absolutist markers) are reported per kill basis
scoring_contract.no_arbitrary_kill_percentage: no threshold on kill counts is defined after seeing results

candidate.mechanism: a static magnetic water conditioner aligned across the supply pipe alters the crystallization kinetics of dissolved calcium carbonate so scale cannot nucleate and deposit in the nozzle throats; precipitation is redirected to suspended non-adhering particles carried through the sprays
candidate.intervention: clamp-on permanent magnet array (0.9 T nominal field, 6 pairs) on the 150 mm cooling-water supply line upstream of the spray header; no contact with the water, no moving parts, no power
candidate.predicted_effect: scale-bound clogging events per campaign reduced by 90 percent (4.1 to below 0.4); thermal-crown variation held inside the 12 micron band without any cleaning
candidate.testable_prediction: coupon-based scaling-rate test on conditioned versus unconditioned recirculated water shows a 90 percent reduction in calcium carbonate deposition mass over a 120-hour campaign-equivalent exposure
candidate.novel_design_variable: magnet pair count and field orientation relative to flow axis
known_failure_modes: loss of field strength at elevated temperature

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: recirculated water at 32-38 C, 14 bar supply, continuous flow; no chemical dosing permitted

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_BAD
ground_truth.defect_class: mechanism failure — no physically valid mechanism: static magnetic fields at ~1 T do not measurably alter dissolved ionic species' precipitation kinetics or nucleation thermodynamics; decades of controlled studies find no reproducible anti-scaling effect beyond trivial residence-time mixing
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The claimed causal chain (static field -> altered crystallization kinetics -> non-adhering precipitate) has no accepted physical mechanism at the stated field strength; the effect size claimed (90 percent) has never been reproduced under controlled conditions. A kill on MECHANISM_FAILURE with any of these markers is a correctly-grounded objection.

candidate.mechanism: acoustic cavitation micro-jetting from piezoelectric transducers bonded to the spray header continuously scours the 3 mm nozzle throats, detaching scale and biofilm deposits before they bridge; cavitation bubbles collapse at 40 kHz and the resulting micro-jets keep throats clean in service
candidate.intervention: six 40 kHz 600 W piezoelectric transducers welded to the header body, one per 20-nozzle segment, powered continuously from the mill's auxiliary supply
candidate.predicted_effect: in-service nozzle clogging eliminated (0 events per campaign); cleaning deferred to annual overhaul; thermal-crown variation inside 6 microns
candidate.testable_prediction: a header segment with transducers active versus inactive shows zero versus 4.1 clogging events per 120-hour campaign in a split-header mill trial
candidate.novel_design_variable: transducer placement density along the header
known_failure_modes: transducer debonding from header vibration environment

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: 14 bar static pressure in the header; water 32-38 C; transducers rated to 70 C and 10 bar differential

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_BAD
ground_truth.defect_class: boundary-condition failure — acoustic cavitation requires the liquid's local static pressure to fall below vapor pressure during rarefaction: at 14 bar static header pressure the required acoustic intensity is orders of magnitude above the transducers' rating, and near-field jetting decays within centimeters while the farthest nozzles sit up to 2 m from any transducer; the mechanism is real only in low-pressure near-field regimes far outside the declared boundary
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: Ultrasonic cleaning physics is real but regime-bound: cavitation thresholds rise steeply with static pressure (Blake threshold); at 14 bar the required intensity exceeds any bonded piezo stack rating, and the agitation that does propagate cannot reach distant throats. The candidate's own declared boundary conditions exclude the regime where its mechanism operates.

candidate.mechanism: clogging is dominated by mill-scale (iron oxide) particles above 200 microns bridging the 3 mm nozzle throats; a 150-micron automatic backflush strainer on the header supply removes the bridging particles at the source, and nozzle clogging between cleanings falls to near zero
candidate.intervention: single-stage 150-micron automatic backflush strainer (motorized brush screen) on the 150 mm header supply line, sized for full design flow
candidate.predicted_effect: clogging events per campaign reduced from 4.1 to below 0.5; the strainer backflushes on differential-pressure rise with no mill stop
candidate.testable_prediction: with the strainer in service, removed-nozzle metallurgical analysis shows no particle bridging above 150 microns and campaign clogging counts fall 8x
candidate.novel_design_variable: strainer micron rating versus nozzle throat bridging size
known_failure_modes: strainer blinding during backflush failures

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: full header flow at 14 bar; recirculated water with scale particles present

evidence_items.title: Metallurgical analysis of 40 clogged nozzles across 6 campaigns: 70 percent of blockages are biofilm-slime AGGREGATES of 20-80 micron particles (mixed scale fines embedded in extracellular polymer), 18 percent are friable slime sheets, only 12 percent are pure scale particles above 200 microns

Recirculation-loop microbiological survey: sessile biofilm coverage on header walls at 10^6 CFU per square centimeter, slime production rate correlated with 32-38 C water temperature, not with scale particle load

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_BAD
ground_truth.defect_class: evidence contradiction — the candidate's premise (clogging dominated by >200 micron scale particles) is directly refuted by the provided nozzle analyses: 88 percent of blockages are biofilm-slime aggregates at 20-80 microns that pass any 150-micron strainer; only 12 percent are the particles the strainer removes
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The provided evidence (ev:metanalysis-40, ev:biofilm-load) directly contradicts the candidate's load model: a 150-micron strainer addresses at most 12 percent of measured blockages. The correct kill binds the objection to the measured 70/18/12 percent split and the 20-80 micron aggregate sizes — not to a generic 'no evidence' assertion.

candidate.mechanism: an intelligent nozzle-health platform fuses spray-pressure telemetry and historical clogging patterns to predict which nozzles will clog and schedule their cleaning exactly when needed, eliminating unnecessary cleaning and the late-campaign crown excursions
candidate.intervention: per-segment pressure sensors plus a cloud analytics subscription; cleaning continues at the same planned roll-change cadence (~120 hours) with the analytics dashboard ranking which nozzles the crew inspects first
candidate.predicted_effect: clogging events per campaign stay at approximately 4 (detected earlier); thermal-crown variation stays at 28 microns late-campaign (same as today); roll-change downtime unchanged at 45 minutes
candidate.testable_prediction: the platform flags 85 percent of clogs at least one shift before the operator would notice them; cleaning cadence, clog count and crown variation are unchanged from the baseline
candidate.novel_design_variable: prediction horizon of the analytics model
known_failure_modes: sensor drift in the header environment

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: same cleaning schedule as the baseline; no water-treatment change; no hardware change to nozzles

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_BAD
ground_truth.defect_class: baseline equivalence — the intervention is the baseline (clean at roll changes, ~120 h cadence) with sensors and a dashboard added; the candidate's own predicted effect EQUALS the baseline on every problem quantity (4.1 clogs, 28 micron excursions, 45 min downtime); nothing new beats the status quo
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: By its own numbers the candidate does not change any problem quantity: clog rate 4.1->~4, crown 28->28, downtime 45->45. A monitoring layer on an unchanged cleaning schedule is the baseline plus telemetry. The correct kill states the equivalence against the candidate's own declared predictions.

candidate.mechanism: every nozzle throat carries an in-line micro-valve with an optical particle sensor; when a particle approaches, the micro-valve diverts flow to a standby throat while an integrated micro-ejector blows the particle back into the header, so no throat ever bridges
candidate.intervention: 120 units of 3 mm in-line micro-valve + optical sorter + micro-ejector assemblies, one per nozzle, with per-nozzle servo control and shared 24 V rails along the header
candidate.predicted_effect: zero clogging events per campaign at full spray uniformity; automatic self-cleaning with no crew involvement
candidate.testable_prediction: a single instrumented nozzle assembly passes a 500-hour abrasive-scale slurry challenge with zero throat blockages and flow stability within 2 percent
candidate.novel_design_variable: micro-valve actuation response time versus particle transit time
known_failure_modes: optical window fouling

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: 3 mm throat geometry, 14 bar, 32-38 C water with abrasive scale fines; mill vibration environment

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_BAD
ground_truth.defect_class: implementation impossibility — 3 mm throat at 14 bar with abrasive scale fines cannot host servo micro-valves, optics and electronics at peak header temperatures; no such 3 mm in-line servo/micro-ejector component class exists or is manufacturable for this service, and 120 of them on a vibrating header fails any reasonable reliability budget
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The assembly class (micro-valve + optical sorter + micro-ejector at 3 mm scale, 14 bar, abrasive service, mill vibration) is beyond any demonstrated or manufacturable component technology; the intervention cannot be built as specified. The correct kill cites the physical/manufacturing impossibility, not merely cost.

candidate.mechanism: vortex-enhanced swirl nozzles create a self-cleaning flow field that improves overall roll-cooling health by 60 percent; the swirling flow centrifuges particles away from the throat wall and enriches the spray's cooling wellness
candidate.intervention: replace all 120 flat-fan nozzles with swirl-vortex nozzles of the same flow class
candidate.predicted_effect: roll-cooling health improves by 60 percent; spray quality feels noticeably better to the mill crew; clogging becomes rare
candidate.testable_prediction: post-retrofit inspection shows the nozzles look cleaner and the crew reports better cooling
candidate.novel_design_variable: swirl chamber helix angle
known_failure_modes: undefined

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: same header supply at 14 bar; same nominal flow per nozzle

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_BAD
ground_truth.defect_class: measurement ambiguity — 'cooling health' and 'cooling wellness' are not measurable quantities; the 60 percent figure has no measurement basis; the testable prediction (nozzles look cleaner, crew reports better) pins no instrument, no acceptance band and no problem quantity (clog events, crown microns); no falsification is possible on the stated prediction
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The candidate never connects its effect to a measurable problem quantity with an instrument and a band; '60 percent' is unanchored. The correct kill identifies the unmeasurable claim and the missing instrument/band, not a fabricated physics objection.

candidate.mechanism: an electrostatic precipitator section charges incoming scale particles and collects them on parallel plates, so particle load reaching the nozzles falls and clogging declines; electrostatic collection is a mature industrial dust-removal technology
candidate.intervention: plate-type electrostatic precipitator spool in the 150 mm supply line (50 kV corona field, 300 mm collection length) ahead of the spray header
candidate.predicted_effect: scale-particle load to the nozzles cut 95 percent; particle-driven clogging events fall from 4.1 per campaign to below 0.2
candidate.testable_prediction: isokinetic particle counts upstream and downstream of the spool show 95 percent removal of particles above 20 microns at design flow
candidate.novel_design_variable: corona field strength versus particle charging efficiency
known_failure_modes: plate fouling with slime

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: water conductivity typical of recirculated mill cooling water; full header flow

ground_truth.label: NEAR_MISS
ground_truth.defect_class: magnitude — electrostatic collection is real (gas-side dust control at 0.5-2 m/s), but in a conductive liquid at the header's ~4.5 m/s flow velocity and 150 mm line, the space-charge screening and collection length needed for 95 percent removal of 20-80 micron particles is tens of meters, not 300 mm; liquid-phase ESP at these scales is orders of magnitude beyond the claimed performance
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The physics exists (electrostatic migration), but the claimed 95 percent removal in 300 mm at 4.5 m/s in conductive water is a magnitude-scale violation: liquid-phase space-charge limits make the claimed collection physically unreachable in the proposed envelope. The correct kill cites the orders-of-magnitude gap between gas-phase ESP practice and this liquid-phase application.

candidate.mechanism: a polymeric scale-inhibitor coating inside the nozzle throats interferes with calcium carbonate nucleation on the wall surface, so adherent scale cannot form; threshold inhibitors (phosphonate-class chemistry) demonstrably slow nucleation in cooling-water service
candidate.intervention: electrostatically applied phosphonate-embedded polymer coating (40 micron layer) on all 120 nozzle throats at each scheduled cleaning
candidate.predicted_effect: adherent scale nucleation in throats suppressed 90 percent; clogging events per campaign fall from 4.1 to below 0.6
candidate.testable_prediction: coated versus uncoated coupon exposure in the recirculated water shows a 90 percent reduction in adherent scale mass after 120 hours
candidate.novel_design_variable: inhibitor loading in the polymer matrix
known_failure_modes: coating abrasion by scale fines

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: throat flow at 14 bar, 32-38 C; water residence in each throat approximately 1-2 ms

ground_truth.label: NEAR_MISS
ground_truth.defect_class: magnitude — threshold inhibition chemistry is real but requires contact times of minutes-to-hours in bulk water at ppm dosing; the water resides in a 3 mm throat for ~1.5 milliseconds, four orders of magnitude too short for surface nucleation kinetics to be affected by a wall coating; the coupon test (hours of immersion) cannot transfer to the in-service timescale
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: Nucleation inhibition is time-scale dependent: bulk-water threshold effects need minutes of contact, the throat provides ~1.5 ms. The correct kill exposes the residence-time / kinetics mismatch (the four-orders-of-magnitude gap), which the candidate's own boundary conditions declare.

candidate.mechanism: continuous low-amplitude vibration of the spray header at 200 Hz prevents particle settling and early deposit consolidation in nozzle inlets; vibration-assisted transport is proven in industrial hoppers and chutes, and deposits never consolidate if the surface never rests
candidate.intervention: two 200 Hz electro-mechanical shakers mounted on the header ends, 12 kW continuous drive, header supported on tuned isolation mounts
candidate.predicted_effect: deposit consolidation in nozzle inlets eliminated; clogging events per campaign fall from 4.1 to below 0.3; no scheduled cleaning needed
candidate.testable_prediction: a bench header section vibrated at 200 Hz versus static shows no deposit consolidation after a 120-hour slurry exposure
candidate.novel_design_variable: vibration amplitude at the nozzle inlets
known_failure_modes: shaker bearing wear

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: header rigidly connected to mill frame at the roll-cooling interface; thermal-crown variation must stay inside 12 microns; 14 bar service

ground_truth.label: NEAR_MISS
ground_truth.defect_class: creates a larger failure mode — hopper vibration works on dry granular transport at rest, but a continuously vibrating header rigidly coupled to the mill frame transmits 200 Hz into the roll-gap environment: the strip-gauge and thermal-crown tolerance (12 microns) cannot survive continuous header vibration, weld-fatigue life at the nozzle seats collapses, and 12 kW continuous drive exceeds the mill's auxiliary budget for a water-spray problem
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The anti-settling effect is real but the intervention destroys the constraint it must preserve: continuous 200 Hz header vibration is incompatible with the declared 12-micron crown band and roll-gap stability, and weld fatigue at the nozzle seats becomes the dominant failure mode. The correct kill cites the constraint violation (the problem's own bound), not a fabricated impossibility.

candidate.mechanism: a two-stage wedge-wire cascade (300 then 120 micron) on the header supply removes scale particles above 120 microns before they reach the nozzles, with dP-triggered automatic backflush keeping the cascade in service without mill stops; the intervention explicitly targets SCALE-PARTICLE clogging only — biofilm clogging is declared OUT OF SCOPE and remains handled by the mill's existing biocide program
candidate.intervention: two-stage wedge-wire cascade with dP transmitters and automatic backflush valves on the 150 mm header supply, sized for full design flow
candidate.predicted_effect: scale-particle-driven clogging events (the 12 percent of measured blockages that are pure scale above 200 microns, plus bridging nuclei) reduced 8x; total campaign clogging events fall from 4.1 to approximately 3.3 (the biofilm share unchanged); the declared scope is partial and stated honestly
candidate.testable_prediction: removed-nozzle analysis over two campaigns shows scale-particle blockages reduced 8x while biofilm blockage counts are statistically unchanged; the partial effect is the declared scope
candidate.novel_design_variable: second-stage micron rating versus bridging nucleus size
known_failure_modes: backflush valve jam (maintained spares held)

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: scale-particle clogging only, above 120 microns; biofilm clogging explicitly out of scope (existing biocide program continues); 13-15 bar supply; no mill stop for installation (flanged spool swap during planned roll change)

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_GOOD_WITH_DECLARED_SCOPE
ground_truth.defect_class: none — a sound, honestly-scoped intervention: the mechanism is standard filtration physics, the prediction is quantified with instruments and bands, the partial effect is declared (12 percent pure-scale share addressed), and the out-of-scope failure mode is disclosed and covered by an existing system. An attacker demanding full biofilm coverage kills via SCOPE_MISMATCH (demanding content the candidate's contract explicitly does not carry — the R445 diagnosis class)
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The candidate's scope declaration is honest and the declared effect is achievable by standard means. Objections of the form 'does not address biofilm' are scope-mismatch objections: the biofilm axis is explicitly out of the declared boundary and handled by the existing program. The correct verdict is SURVIVED (at most a RISK note on the partial coverage).

candidate.mechanism: raising header flow 20 percent using existing pump headroom increases convective flushing velocity through each nozzle throat, raising the particle size that can be transported through without settling; the intervention is declared valid ONLY for campaigns with strip entry temperature below 85 C (the pump curve and thermal balance at higher entry temperatures exceed the declared envelope)
candidate.intervention: supply valve setpoint change plus a strip-entry-temperature interlock that reverts flow to nominal above 85 C; no hardware change
candidate.predicted_effect: for in-envelope campaigns (about 70 percent of the mill's campaign mix), clogging events fall from 4.1 to approximately 2.8 and crown excursions shrink; out-of-envelope campaigns revert to baseline behavior honestly
candidate.testable_prediction: in-envelope campaigns measure a clogging-event reduction to approximately 2.8 with 95 percent confidence band 2.4-3.2; out-of-envelope campaigns measure no significant change from 4.1
candidate.novel_design_variable: flow boost fraction versus throat transport velocity
known_failure_modes: higher flow increases abrasive wear on throat edges (measured wear budget recalculated and inside the roll-change interval)

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: strip entry temperature below 85 C only; header pressure stays 13-15 bar; pump headroom of 22 percent exists per pump curve; out-of-envelope reversion is automatic

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_GOOD_WITH_DECLARED_SCOPE
ground_truth.defect_class: none — a bounded operational change with an explicit temperature envelope, an automatic out-of-envelope reversion, quantified in-envelope effect with confidence band, and honestly-declared wear trade-off. An attacker demanding performance at 95 C entry temperature or calling the 85 C envelope a defect kills via SCOPE_MISMATCH — the candidate's own boundary excludes that regime
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The candidate does what it declares inside its envelope and reverts honestly outside it. Objections demanding full-envelope performance are out-of-scope demands (the R445 SCOPE_MISMATCH class). The correct verdict is SURVIVED.

candidate.mechanism: each nozzle position carries a standby twin on a dual-manifold block; a per-position dP sensor detects throat bridging and a fast three-way valve shifts that position to the standby twin within 0.4 seconds; the roll's measured thermal inertia carries the flow through the 0.4 s switchover transient with a computed crown perturbation of 1.1 microns (inside the 12 micron band with margin)
candidate.intervention: dual-manifold nozzle blocks with per-position dP sensing and fast-redundancy valves, phased in over three planned roll changes (no mill stop)
candidate.predicted_effect: clogging events reaching the strip fall to zero (every bridge is bypassed in-service); cleaning consolidates into the annual overhaul; crown variation stays inside the 12 micron band including the switchover transients
candidate.testable_prediction: injected partial blockages during a production campaign are bypassed within 0.4 s each, with measured crown perturbation below 2 microns per event and cumulative below 4 microns per campaign
candidate.novel_design_variable: standby valve actuation time versus roll thermal inertia budget
known_failure_modes: three-way valve sticking (position-redundant sensors cross-check)

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: 13-15 bar; 32-38 C water; the 0.4 s transient budget is inside the measured roll thermal-inertia limit; one standby per position (a simultaneous double failure is out of scope, handled by the scheduled cleaning floor)

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_GOOD_WITH_DECLARED_SCOPE
ground_truth.defect_class: none — a sound redundancy design with a computed transient budget inside the declared crown band, an honest out-of-scope double-failure declaration, and a phased no-mill-stop installation. An attacker demanding 'zero crown perturbation during switchover' or simultaneous-failure coverage kills via SCOPE_MISMATCH (demanding performance outside the declared budget)
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The transient is quantified (1.1 microns vs the 12 micron band) and the double-failure regime is explicitly excluded with a fallback. Objections escalating the declared 0.4 s transient to a kill ignore the computed thermal-inertia budget — the R445 SEVERITY_INFLATION/SCOPE_MISMATCH pattern. The correct verdict is SURVIVED.

candidate.mechanism: a two-stage inertial wedge-wire cascade (300 then 120 micron) on the header supply removes scale particles and aggregate nuclei above 120 microns; dP transmitters on both stages trigger an automatic backflush (reverse-flow + mechanical brush) that restores full flow without mill stop; combined with the mill's existing biocide program, both clogging axes are addressed at their measured sources
candidate.intervention: two-stage wedge-wire cascade + dP monitoring + automatic backflush valves on the 150 mm supply, installed as a flanged spool swap during a planned roll change
candidate.predicted_effect: campaign clogging events fall from 4.1 to below 1.5 (scale-nucleus share suppressed 8x, biofilm share carried by the existing biocide program); late-campaign crown excursions fall from 28 to below 16 microns; roll-change cleaning time drops to 15 minutes
candidate.testable_prediction: two-campaign split trial: cascade-in-service arm measures clogging events 1.5 or below with 95 percent confidence band 1.0-2.0, versus the baseline arm at 4.1 plus or minus 0.6; dP-triggered backflush events logged per stage; crown variation measured by the mill's existing roll-thermography system
candidate.novel_design_variable: second-stage micron rating and backflush dP threshold
known_failure_modes: backflush valve jam (maintained spare held at the mill)
fine-passive slimes crossing both stages (addressed by the biocide program, measured share 18 percent)

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: 13-15 bar supply; full design flow; recirculated water with scale particles present; no mill stop for installation or operation

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_GOOD
ground_truth.defect_class: none — a sound control: standard filtration physics, quantified prediction with instruments, confidence band and baseline comparison, honest failure modes including the residual slime share, effect beats the baseline on the problem quantities within the declared constraints
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: Quantified prediction with instrument and acceptance band; physics consistent with the regime (inertial screening at the cascade's channel Reynolds numbers); predicted effect beats the baseline on every problem quantity; constraints honored (no mill stop, pressure band held).

candidate.mechanism: a hydrocyclone pre-separator on the recirculation RETURN line (before the cooling basin) centrifuges scale particles above 100 microns out of the loop continuously, so the recirculated particle concentration decays campaign-over-campaign instead of accumulating; the basin's existing settling volume finishes the separation
candidate.intervention: one 150 mm hydrocyclone on the return line with an automated underflow collection pot, backflushed to a scale skip at each roll change
candidate.predicted_effect: loop particle concentration above 100 microns falls 85 percent within two campaigns; scale-driven clogging events fall from 4.1 to approximately 2.6; no pressure-drop penalty on the supply side (the cyclone sits on the return)
candidate.testable_prediction: isokinetic particle counts on return and basin-outlet lines show 85 percent plus or minus 5 percent removal above 100 microns at design flow; campaign clog counts trend to 2.6 plus or minus 0.5 over two campaigns
candidate.novel_design_variable: cyclone apex diameter versus cut size at return flow
known_failure_modes: apex plugging during episodic descaling dumps (bypass protects supply)

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: return-line installation only; 13-15 bar supply untouched; basin settling volume available

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_GOOD
ground_truth.defect_class: none — a sound control: standard hydrocyclone physics, quantified removal with band, supply-side constraints untouched by construction, honest episodic-dump failure mode with bypass
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: Standard separation physics with a measured removal claim, confidence band, and a failure mode that cannot damage the supply constraint (return-side installation).

candidate.mechanism: a nozzle geometry with a 6 mm throat (double the current 3 mm) and an internal swirl ramp replaces sharp throat entry corners with a converging spiral passage; the doubled throat raises the bridging particle size threshold by roughly 4x (bridging scales with throat-to-particle ratio) and the swirl passage prevents low-velocity dead zones at the wall where deposits nucleate
candidate.intervention: nozzle replacement with 6 mm-throat swirl-ramp flat-fan nozzles of equivalent spray angle; spray distribution re-verified by the nozzle vendor's patternator at the mill's supply pressure
candidate.predicted_effect: campaign clogging events fall from 4.1 to approximately 1.8 (bridging threshold shift); droplet coarsening of approximately 8 percent is measured and offset by a 5 percent flow increase that stays inside the pump's headroom; crown variation inside 12 microns maintained by the re-patterned distribution

candidate.novel_design_variable: throat diameter to bridging threshold ratio
known_failure_modes: slightly coarser droplet spectrum (measured, offset declared)
swirl ramp wear (vendor wear-life certificate for abrasive service)

constraint_set.boundary_conditions: 14 bar supply; same nominal flow class; roll-change-window installation; spray pattern uniformity within 5 percent of current

ground_truth.label: KNOWN_GOOD
ground_truth.defect_class: none — a sound control: standard fluid-mechanics reasoning (bridging threshold scaling), a measured trade-off declared (coarser droplets, offset within pump headroom), vendor-verified spray pattern, quantified band
ground_truth.ground_truth_basis: The mechanism is ordinary engineering (larger throat, no dead zones), the trade-offs are measured and declared, and the prediction is instrumented with bands. Nothing is asserted without basis.

candidate.mechanism: the measured 88 percent biofilm-slime share of blockages is addressable by chemistry the mill already permits: a continuous low-dose oxidizing biocide plus a weekly dispersant slug oxidizes sessile biofilm and strips extracellular polymer from header walls, so slime aggregates never grow to bridging size at the throats
candidate.intervention: dosing skid on the recirculation loop (already plumbed for pH correction): continuous 0.3 ppm actinic biocide with ORP control, weekly 15-minute dispersant slug at 8 ppm with automatic rinse-down; dosing rates inside the mill's existing discharge permit
candidate.predicted_effect: sessile biofilm coverage falls from 10^6 to below 10^4 CFU per square centimeter within three weeks; biofilm-share clogging events fall from 2.9 to below 0.6 per campaign; total campaign clogging events fall from 4.1 to approximately 1.4 combined with routine screening
candidate.testable_prediction: monthly header-wall swab cultures show the 2-order CFU reduction; campaign clog counts over two campaigns measure 1.4 plus or minus 0.5; discharge permit compliance verified by the existing effluent monitoring
candidate.novel_design_variable: dispersant slug frequency versus slime regrowth rate

biocide demand spikes from oil leaks in the loop (alarm + manual slug)
